newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp bids 435 DM/shr for Thyssen.
newsitem.headline: Krupp bids 435 DM/shr for Thyssen.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Krupp said on Tuesday it would offer Thyssen shareholders 435 marks a share, a 25 percent premium on Monday's closing share price, in a rare hostile takeover bid.
"This is the pre-condition needed in order to later merge Krupp and Thyssen into a powerful internationally competitive enterprise," Krupp said in a statement.

Contrary to analysts' expectations, Krupp said it would make a cash offer that would be secured by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment arm of Deutsche Bank AG, Dresdner Bank, U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs and other unidentified institutions.
Krupp explained the move by saying that as the world economy becomes more intertwined it was crucial for companies to cut costs in production, logistics and distribution.

"That's why it is indispensable to achieve sufficient size in business areas in accordance with global standards. Only under these conditions do German companies have the chance to survive in interational competition," the company said.

Krupp said further that in order to achieve its goal of a merger with Thyssen, it was first necessary to acquire a controlling majority of the company's capital. It added that 70 percent of the two firms' businesses were complementary."
